name: JPEG
description: JPEG/JFIF Image File Format. JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Group) is the most common lossy image compression format. Files are structured as a sequence of marker segments, each starting with a 0xFF byte followed by a type byte.
author: HexMarksTheSpot
forensic_notes:
**JPEG Forensic Analysis Guide**

**What is JPEG?**
JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Group) is the most widely used lossy image compression format, found on nearly every digital camera, smartphone, and website. JPEG files use the JFIF (JPEG File Interchange Format) or Exif (Exchangeable Image File Format) container to store compressed image data alongside metadata.

**Why JPEG is forensically important:**
JPEG images are among the most commonly encountered digital evidence. They appear in:
- Digital camera and smartphone photos (crime scenes, surveillance, child exploitation)
- Screenshots and document scans
- Web downloads and social media
- Email attachments
- USB drives, cloud storage, and messaging apps

**Key Forensic Analysis Areas:**

1. **Exif Metadata (APP1 segment)**
   - **Camera identification:** Make, model, serial number, lens info
   - **GPS coordinates:** Latitude/longitude embedded by smartphones and GPS-enabled cameras
   - **Timestamps:** DateTimeOriginal (shutter press), DateTimeDigitized, DateTime (last save)
   - **Software field:** Reveals editing tools (Photoshop, GIMP, etc.)
   - **Thumbnail:** May retain the ORIGINAL image even after the main image was cropped or edited
   - *Forensic tip:* Compare the Exif thumbnail with the main image — differences prove editing

2. **Quantization Tables (DQT segment)**
   - Act as a **fingerprint** for the encoding software or camera
   - Standard tables can identify: Photoshop, ImageMagick, libjpeg, specific camera models
   - Double compression artifacts: If an image is opened and re-saved, the quantization tables change
   - Tools: `JPEGsnoop` can identify the source application from DQT tables

3. **Image Manipulation Detection**
   - **Error Level Analysis (ELA):** Re-saving at a known quality and comparing error levels reveals edited regions
   - **Chroma subsampling mismatch:** Different subsampling between Exif data and SOF header suggests re-encoding
   - **Missing or stripped metadata:** Social media platforms strip Exif (Facebook, Twitter) — presence/absence reveals sharing history
   - **Inconsistent compression:** Different quality levels in different parts of an image suggest splicing

4. **Steganography Detection**
   - **After-EOI data:** Any data appended after the `FF D9` End of Image marker is suspicious (appended ZIPs, hidden messages)
   - **Comment segments (COM):** May contain hidden messages or tool signatures
   - **LSB steganography:** Tools like StegDetect, OutGuess, and F5 embed data in DCT coefficients
   - **Unusual APP segments:** Non-standard application markers may carry hidden payloads

5. **Metadata Stripping and Anti-Forensics**
   - Exif removal tools: `exiftool -all=`, Metadata Anonymisation Toolkit
   - Re-encoding strips original quantization tables
   - Screenshot conversion: Taking a screenshot of an image creates a 'clean' copy with new metadata
   - *Forensic tip:* Even stripped images retain quantization table fingerprints from the LAST encoder used

**Common Investigation Workflow:**
1. Check SOI marker integrity (file not truncated at start?)
2. Extract and analyze all Exif metadata (timestamps, GPS, device info)
3. Compare Exif thumbnail with main image
4. Identify encoding software from quantization tables
5. Check for data after EOI marker (steganography, appended files)
6. Look for evidence of re-compression (double quantization artifacts)
7. Cross-reference timestamps with file system metadata ($MFT, $UsnJrnl)

fields.name: SOI_Marker
fields.description:
**Start of Image (SOI)**

Always `FF D8`. This 2-byte marker identifies the beginning of every JPEG file.

*Forensic Value:* Signature verification. A valid JPEG must start with FF D8. Absence or corruption of this marker may indicate file damage or deliberate manipulation.

fields.name: Segment
fields.description:
**JPEG Marker Segments**

JPEG files are composed of a series of marker segments. Each segment begins with a 2-byte marker (FF xx), followed by a 2-byte length field and segment-specific data. The length field includes itself but not the marker.

Segments continue until the Start of Scan (SOS / FF DA) marker is reached, after which the compressed image data follows.

fields.name: SegmentMarker
fields.description:
**Segment Marker**

A 2-byte marker identifying the segment type. All markers start with `0xFF` followed by a type byte.

Common markers:
- `FF E0` (APP0) — JFIF header
- `FF E1` (APP1) — Exif / XMP metadata
- `FF DB` (DQT) — Quantization tables
- `FF C0` (SOF0) — Baseline DCT frame
- `FF C4` (DHT) — Huffman tables
- `FF DA` (SOS) — Start of Scan (compressed data follows)
- `FF FE` (COM) — Comment
- `FF DD` (DRI) — Define Restart Interval

value_map.65473: SOF1 - Start of Frame (Extended Sequential DCT)

fields.name: SegmentLength
fields.description:
**Segment Length**

Length of this segment in bytes, including this 2-byte length field but excluding the 2-byte marker.

To get the data-only length, subtract 2.

fields.name: JFIF_Data
fields.description:
**APP0 — JFIF Header**

The JFIF (JPEG File Interchange Format) segment provides basic image metadata including version, pixel density, and optional thumbnail. This is the standard first segment after SOI for JFIF-compliant files.

fields.name: JFIF_Identifier
fields.description:
**JFIF Identifier**

ASCII string `JFIF` followed by a null byte (`4A 46 49 46 00`). Identifies this APP0 segment as a JFIF header.

fields.name: JFIF_VersionMajor
fields.description:
**JFIF Major Version**

Major version number of the JFIF specification. Typically `1`.

fields.name: JFIF_VersionMinor
fields.description:
**JFIF Minor Version**

Minor version number (e.g., `02` for version 1.02).

Known versions: 1.00, 1.01, 1.02.

fields.name: DensityUnits
fields.description:
**Pixel Density Units**

Specifies the unit of measurement for Xdensity and Ydensity.

*Forensic Value:* Discrepancies in density settings may indicate image editing or manipulation.

fields.name: Xdensity
fields.description:
**Horizontal Pixel Density**

Horizontal pixel density. Must not be zero.

Common values: 72 or 96 DPI for screen, 150-600 DPI for print.

fields.name: Ydensity
fields.description:
**Vertical Pixel Density**

Vertical pixel density. Must not be zero.

fields.name: Xthumbnail
fields.description:
**Thumbnail Width**

Width of the optional embedded thumbnail in pixels. Zero means no thumbnail.

fields.name: Ythumbnail
fields.description:
**Thumbnail Height**

Height of the optional embedded thumbnail in pixels. Zero means no thumbnail.

fields.name: JFIF_ThumbnailData
fields.description:
**Thumbnail Image Data**

Uncompressed 24-bit RGB raster data for the thumbnail. Size = 3 x Xthumbnail x Ythumbnail bytes.

*Forensic Value:* The embedded thumbnail may retain the original image content even if the main image was edited (thumbnail not updated).

fields.name: Exif_Data
fields.description:
**APP1 — Exif / XMP Metadata**

Contains Exchangeable Image File Format (Exif) metadata or XMP (Extensible Metadata Platform) data.

*Forensic Value:* **Extremely valuable.** Exif data often contains:
- Camera make, model, serial number
- GPS coordinates (latitude/longitude)
- Original creation timestamp
- Software used for editing
- Thumbnail of the original image
- Lens information, exposure settings
- Unique image identifiers

Exif data persists through many image operations and can reveal editing history, device identification, and geographic location.

fields.name: Exif_Identifier
fields.description:
**Exif Identifier**

ASCII string `Exif` followed by two null bytes (`45 78 69 66 00 00`), or `http:` for XMP data.

*Forensic Value:* Identifies whether this is Exif or XMP metadata.

fields.name: TIFF_ByteOrder
fields.description:
**TIFF Byte Order Mark**

Determines endianness for ALL subsequent TIFF/Exif fields:
- `49 49` (0x4949 = 18761) — Intel byte order (little-endian). Most common on cameras and smartphones.
- `4D 4D` (0x4D4D = 19789) — Motorola byte order (big-endian). Used by some older cameras and scanners.

*Forensic Value:* The byte order reveals the hardware lineage of the device that wrote the Exif data. Intel byte order (little-endian) is standard for modern consumer devices. Motorola (big-endian) may indicate older hardware, specific camera brands, or non-standard software.

fields.name: TIFF_LE
fields.description:
**TIFF Structure (Little-Endian)**

The Exif data is wrapped in a TIFF container. This section parses the TIFF header and IFD0 (Image File Directory 0) entries using Intel/little-endian byte order.

fields.name: TIFF_Magic
fields.description:
**TIFF Magic Number**

Always `0x002A` (42). Confirms this is a valid TIFF structure.

fields.name: IFD0_Offset
fields.description:
**IFD0 Offset**

Byte offset from the start of the TIFF header (the byte order mark) to the first IFD. Typically `0x00000008` (immediately after the 8-byte TIFF header).

*Forensic Value:* A non-standard offset (not 8) may indicate tools that rewrite Exif data or deliberate manipulation.

fields.name: IFD0_EntryCount
fields.description:
**IFD0 Entry Count**

Number of 12-byte tag entries in IFD0. Each entry describes one piece of metadata (camera make, model, timestamp, image dimensions, etc.). Typical range: 10–30 entries for camera images.

fields.name: IFD0 Tag ${_count}
fields.description:
**IFD0 Tag Entry ${_count}** — 12-byte TIFF tag entry containing a metadata field identifier, data type, count, and value or offset to the value.

**Key forensic tags to look for:**
- 0x010F (271): Camera Make
- 0x0110 (272): Camera Model
- 0x0112 (274): Orientation
- 0x011A (282): XResolution
- 0x011B (283): YResolution
- 0x0128 (296): ResolutionUnit
- 0x0131 (305): Software
- 0x0132 (306): DateTime (last modification)
- 0x013B (315): Artist
- 0x8298 (33432): Copyright
- 0x8769 (34665): Exif IFD Pointer
- 0x8825 (34853): GPS IFD Pointer

fields.name: TagID
fields.description: **Tag ID** — Identifies which piece of metadata this entry contains.

fields.name: TagType
fields.description: **Data Type** — TIFF data type code determining how to interpret the value field.

fields.name: TagCount
fields.description: **Value Count** — Number of values of the specified type. For ASCII strings, this is the character count including the null terminator.

fields.name: TagValue
fields.description:
**Value / Offset** — If the data fits in 4 bytes, the value is stored here directly (left-justified for types smaller than 4 bytes). Otherwise, this field contains a byte offset from the TIFF header start to where the actual data is stored.

**Inline values** (data ≤ 4 bytes):
- SHORT with count ≤ 2: values packed here
- LONG with count 1: value stored directly
- ASCII with count ≤ 4: string stored here

**Offset values** (data > 4 bytes):
- ASCII strings (Make, Model, DateTime, Software)
- RATIONAL values (GPS coordinates, resolution)
- Large data blocks (thumbnail, MakerNote)

*Forensic note:* When this is an offset, add it to the TIFF header start position (APP1 data start + 6 bytes for 'Exif\0\0') to get the absolute file position.

fields.name: IFD0_NextOffset
fields.description:
**Next IFD Offset**

Byte offset from TIFF header to the next IFD (typically IFD1 containing thumbnail metadata). Zero means no more IFDs.

*Forensic Value:* IFD1 usually contains the thumbnail image — compare with the main image to detect editing. Non-zero values point to the thumbnail IFD.

fields.name: IFD0_TrailingData
fields.description:
**IFD Data Area & Additional IFDs**

Contains:
- **Tag values too large for 4 bytes** — ASCII strings (Make, Model, DateTime, Software), RATIONAL values (GPS coordinates, XResolution, YResolution), binary blobs (MakerNote, UserComment)
- **Exif Sub-IFD** — Extended Exif tags (ExposureTime, FNumber, DateTimeOriginal, DateTimeDigitized, ShutterSpeed, Aperture, ISO, FocalLength, ExifVersion, FlashPixVersion, ColorSpace, PixelDimensions, SensingMethod, FileSource, SceneType, WhiteBalance, DigitalZoom, FocalLength35mm, SerialNumber, LensInfo, LensModel)
- **GPS Sub-IFD** — GPS tags (GPSLatitudeRef N/S, GPSLatitude, GPSLongitudeRef E/W, GPSLongitude, GPSAltitudeRef, GPSAltitude, GPSTimeStamp, GPSSatellites, GPSMapDatum, GPSDateStamp)
- **IFD1 (Thumbnail IFD)** — Thumbnail metadata and JPEG thumbnail data
- **MakerNote** — Camera manufacturer-specific binary data (Canon, Nikon, Sony, etc.)

*Forensic Value:* **Critical.** This data area contains the most forensically valuable metadata: timestamps, GPS coordinates, camera identification, software signatures, and the Exif thumbnail (which may retain the original unedited image content).

fields.name: TIFF_BE
fields.description:
**TIFF Structure (Big-Endian)**

The Exif data is wrapped in a TIFF container using Motorola/big-endian byte order. This is less common but used by some older cameras and scanners.

fields.name: TIFF_Magic
fields.description:
**TIFF Magic Number**

Always `0x002A` (42). Confirms this is a valid TIFF structure.

fields.name: IFD0_Offset
fields.description:
**IFD0 Offset**

Byte offset from the start of the TIFF header to the first IFD. Typically `0x00000008`.

fields.name: IFD0_EntryCount
fields.description:
**IFD0 Entry Count**

Number of 12-byte tag entries in IFD0.

fields.name: IFD0 Tag ${_count}
fields.description: **IFD0 Tag Entry ${_count}** — 12-byte TIFF tag entry (big-endian).

fields.name: TagID
fields.description: **Tag ID** — Identifies which piece of metadata this entry contains.

fields.name: TagType
fields.description: **Data Type** — TIFF data type code.

fields.name: TagCount
fields.description: **Value Count** — Number of values of the specified type.

fields.name: TagValue
fields.description:
**Value / Offset** — If the data fits in 4 bytes, the value is stored here directly. Otherwise, this is a byte offset from the TIFF header start to the actual data.

*Forensic note:* When an offset, add it to the TIFF header start position (APP1 data start + 6 bytes for 'Exif\0\0') to get the absolute file position.

fields.name: IFD0_NextOffset
fields.description:
**Next IFD Offset**

Byte offset from TIFF header to the next IFD (IFD1 / thumbnail). Zero = no more IFDs.

*Forensic Value:* IFD1 usually contains the thumbnail — compare with main image to detect editing.

fields.name: IFD0_TrailingData
fields.description:
**IFD Data Area & Additional IFDs**

Contains tag values too large for 4 bytes (strings, rationals, binary data), Exif Sub-IFD, GPS Sub-IFD, IFD1 thumbnail metadata, and MakerNote data.

*Forensic Value:* **Critical.** Contains timestamps, GPS coordinates, camera identification, software signatures, and the Exif thumbnail.

fields._comment: --- Fallback: XMP data or unrecognized Exif ---
fields.name: Exif_FallbackPayload
fields.description:
**XMP or Non-Standard APP1 Payload**

This APP1 segment does not contain a standard TIFF/Exif structure (byte order mark is neither `II` nor `MM`). It may contain:
- **XMP metadata** — XML-based metadata (starts with `http://ns.adobe.com/xap/1.0/`)
- **Non-standard APP1 data** — proprietary metadata from specific applications

*Forensic Value:* XMP data may contain Dublin Core metadata (title, creator, description), Photoshop editing history, and camera raw processing settings.

fields.name: APP2_Data
fields.description:
**APP2 — ICC Color Profile**

Contains ICC color management data or FlashPix extensions.

fields.name: APP2_Payload
fields.description:
**ICC Profile Data**

Color profile data for accurate color reproduction. Often starts with `ICC_PROFILE` identifier.

*Forensic Value:* May reveal the software or device that created the color profile.

fields.name: APP12_Data
fields.description:
**APP12 — PictureInfo / Ducky**

Contains PictureInfo or Ducky quality/comment data, often inserted by Adobe Photoshop.

fields.name: APP12_Payload
fields.description:
**PictureInfo / Ducky Data**

Application-specific metadata. Adobe Photoshop uses this for "Save for Web" quality settings.

*Forensic Value:* Reveals Adobe software usage and editing workflow.

fields.name: APP13_Data
fields.description:
**APP13 — Photoshop IRB / IPTC**

Contains Photoshop Image Resource Blocks and IPTC (International Press Telecommunications Council) metadata.

*Forensic Value:* IPTC data includes author, copyright, captions, keywords, and creation date. Photoshop IRBs reveal detailed editing history.

fields.name: APP13_Identifier
fields.description:
**Photoshop Identifier**

Typically `Photoshop 3.0` followed by a null byte.

fields.name: APP13_Payload
fields.description:
**Photoshop IRB / IPTC Payload**

Image Resource Blocks containing IPTC-NAA records, resolution info, print flags, etc.

*Forensic Value:* May contain author name, copyright info, captions, keyword tags, and editing software details.

fields.name: APP14_Data
fields.description:
**APP14 — Adobe DCT Filter**

Adobe-specific segment for color transform information.

fields.name: Adobe_Identifier
fields.description:
**Adobe Identifier**

ASCII string `Adobe`.

fields.name: Adobe_Version
fields.description:
**Adobe DCT Version**

Version of Adobe DCT filter.

fields.name: Adobe_Flags0
fields.description: **Flags 0**

fields.name: Adobe_Flags1
fields.description: **Flags 1**

fields.name: Adobe_ColorTransform
fields.description:
**Color Transform**

Specifies the color encoding used.

fields.name: Comment_Data
fields.description:
**COM — Comment**

A free-text comment embedded in the JPEG file.

*Forensic Value:* Comments may contain author information, software identifiers, timestamps, or hidden messages. Some steganography tools embed data here.

fields.name: Comment_Text
fields.description:
**Comment Text**

Free-form ASCII text. May contain:
- Software name and version (e.g., image editors)
- Author or copyright information
- Creation tool identifier
- Hidden data (steganography)

*Forensic Value:* Can identify the tool used to create or edit the image.

fields.name: DQT_Data
fields.description:
**DQT — Define Quantization Table**

Defines one or more quantization tables used in JPEG compression. These tables control the trade-off between image quality and file size.

*Forensic Value:* Quantization tables are characteristic of specific cameras and software. They can be used to fingerprint the encoding application or identify recompression.

fields.name: QT_PrecisionAndID
fields.description:
**Precision & Table ID**

Packed byte containing:
- **High nibble (bits 4-7):** Precision — `0` = 8-bit values, `1` = 16-bit values
- **Low nibble (bits 0-3):** Table ID — `0` to `3` (typically 0 = luminance, 1 = chrominance)

Common values:
- `0x00` (0) — 8-bit precision, table 0 (luminance / Y)
- `0x01` (1) — 8-bit precision, table 1 (chrominance / CbCr)
- `0x10` (16) — 16-bit precision, table 0

*Forensic Value:* **Important.** Most consumer JPEG images use 8-bit precision (value 0x00 or 0x01). 16-bit precision is rare and may indicate professional, medical, or specialized imaging software.

fields.name: QT_Values
fields.description:
**Quantization Table Values**

64 coefficient values in zig-zag scan order (8-bit: 64 bytes; 16-bit: 128 bytes). These values determine how much each DCT frequency component is divided during compression.

**Forensic fingerprinting:**
- The exact quantization values form a **unique fingerprint** of the encoding tool or camera:
  - **Photoshop:** Has distinctive quality-level-dependent tables
  - **libjpeg/IJG:** Uses a scaled version of the standard Annex K tables
  - **Camera-specific:** Many cameras use proprietary tables unique to their firmware
  - **ImageMagick, GIMP:** Each tool produces identifiable patterns
- **Double compression detection:** If an image was opened and re-saved, the quantization tables will differ from the original encoder's tables
- **Quality level estimation:** Lower values = higher quality, higher values = more compression

*Forensic Value:* **Critical.** Cross-reference quantization values against known databases (JPEGsnoop, Hackerfactor FotoForensics) to identify the source application or camera model. Mismatched tables between images claiming to be from the same source indicate different origins or editing.

fields.name: SOF0_Data
fields.description:
**SOF0/SOF1 — Start of Frame (Sequential DCT)**

Defines the image dimensions, color depth, and component configuration.

- **SOF0** (0xFFC0) — Baseline DCT: The most common JPEG compression. 8-bit precision, Huffman coding.
- **SOF1** (0xFFC1) — Extended Sequential DCT: Supports 8-bit or 12-bit precision. Used by some scanners and medical imaging devices.

*Forensic Value:* SOF1 (extended) is uncommon in consumer photos — its presence may indicate medical imaging, scanning, or specialized capture equipment.

fields.name: SOF_Precision
fields.description:
**Sample Precision**

Bits per sample (typically 8). Specifies the precision of the image components.

fields.name: SOF_ImageHeight
fields.description:
**Image Height**

Height of the image in pixels.

*Forensic Value:* Compare with file metadata and actual rendered dimensions to detect manipulation.

fields.name: SOF_ImageWidth
fields.description:
**Image Width**

Width of the image in pixels.

*Forensic Value:* Compare with file metadata and actual rendered dimensions to detect manipulation.

fields.name: SOF_NumComponents
fields.description:
**Number of Components**

Number of color components in the image.

fields.name: SOF Component ${_count}
fields.description:
**Component ${_count} Specification**

Defines the properties of color component ${_count} — component ID, chroma subsampling factors, and which quantization table to use.

fields.name: SOF_CompID
fields.description:
**Component Identifier**

Identifies which color channel this specification describes.

fields.name: SOF_SamplingFactor
fields.description:
**Sampling Factors**

Packed byte containing horizontal (high nibble) and vertical (low nibble) sampling factors.

Common values and their subsampling ratios:
- `0x22` — 4:2:0 (2×2). Most common on cameras and web. Maximum compression.
- `0x21` — 4:2:2 (2×1). Horizontal subsampling only. Better quality.
- `0x11` — 4:4:4 (1×1). No subsampling. Full chroma resolution. Used by Photoshop at max quality.
- `0x12` — Vertical-only subsampling (uncommon)

*Forensic Value:* **Important.** The chroma subsampling ratio reveals encoding choices:
- **4:2:0 (0x22)** is standard for cameras and most software
- **4:4:4 (0x11)** suggests high-quality professional software (Photoshop, GIMP at max quality)
- **Mismatch between Exif subsampling and SOF subsampling** indicates the image was re-encoded
- **Non-standard ratios** may indicate specialized or modified encoding tools

fields.name: SOF_QTableID
fields.description:
**Quantization Table Selector**

Index of the DQT quantization table used for this component (0–3). Typically:
- Component Y uses table 0 (luminance)
- Components Cb/Cr use table 1 (chrominance)

*Forensic Value:* Unusual table assignments may indicate custom encoding or manipulation.

fields.name: SOF2_Data
fields.description:
**SOF2/SOF3 — Start of Frame (Progressive / Lossless)**

- **SOF2** (0xFFC2) — Progressive DCT: Image data is stored in multiple scans of increasing detail, allowing progressive rendering. Common in web-optimized JPEGs (Photoshop 'Save for Web').
- **SOF3** (0xFFC3) — Lossless: Predictive coding without DCT, preserving exact pixel values. Used in medical imaging (DICOM) and scientific applications.

*Forensic Value:* Progressive encoding (SOF2) suggests web optimization or specific software. Lossless (SOF3) is rare and strongly indicates medical/scientific origin.

fields.name: SOF2_Precision
fields.description:
**Sample Precision**

Bits per sample.

fields.name: SOF2_ImageHeight
fields.description: **Image Height** (pixels)

fields.name: SOF2_ImageWidth
fields.description: **Image Width** (pixels)

fields.name: SOF2_NumComponents
fields.description: **Number of Components**

fields.name: SOF2 Component ${_count}
fields.description: **Component ${_count} Specification** (Progressive/Lossless)

fields.name: SOF2_CompID
fields.description: **Component Identifier**

fields.name: SOF2_SamplingFactor
fields.description:
**Sampling Factors** — High nibble: horizontal, Low nibble: vertical.

*Forensic Value:* Progressive JPEG subsampling reveals the encoding tool's settings.

fields.name: SOF2_QTableID
fields.description: **Quantization Table Selector** (0–3)

fields.name: DHT_Data
fields.description:
**DHT — Define Huffman Table**

Defines Huffman coding tables for entropy encoding of the DCT coefficients.

fields.name: HuffmanTable
fields.description:
**Huffman Table Data**

One or more Huffman tables:
- 1 byte header: class (high nibble: 0=DC, 1=AC) and table ID (low nibble: 0-3)
- 16 bytes: number of codes of each length (1-16 bits)
- Variable: the Huffman values

*Forensic Value:* Like quantization tables, Huffman tables can fingerprint the encoding software.

fields.name: DRI_Data
fields.description:
**DRI — Define Restart Interval**

Specifies the number of MCUs (Minimum Coded Units) between restart markers in the compressed data.

fields.name: RestartInterval
fields.description:
**Restart Interval**

Number of MCUs between RST markers. A value of 0 disables restart markers.

fields.name: SOS_Data
fields.description:
**SOS — Start of Scan**

Marks the beginning of the compressed image data. The scan header specifies which components are included.

After this header, the entropy-coded (compressed) image data follows until the End of Image (EOI / FF D9) marker.

fields.name: SOS_NumComponents
fields.description:
**Number of Components in Scan**

Number of image components in this scan. Typically 1 (grayscale) or 3 (color).

fields.name: SOS_ComponentSpec
fields.description:
**Scan Component Specifications**

For each component (2 bytes each):
- Component selector (1 byte): matches the component ID from SOF
- Huffman table selectors (1 byte): high nibble = DC table, low nibble = AC table

fields.name: SOS_SpectralStart
fields.description:
**Spectral Selection Start**

Start of spectral selection (0 for baseline, 0-63 for progressive).

fields.name: SOS_SpectralEnd
fields.description:
**Spectral Selection End**

End of spectral selection (63 for baseline).

fields.name: SOS_ApproxBitPos
fields.description:
**Successive Approximation Bit Position**

High nibble = successive approximation high bit, low nibble = low bit. Both 0 for baseline.

fields.name: GenericAPP_Data
fields.description:
**Application-Specific Segment**

Contains application-specific data not covered by the known APP segment handlers.

*Forensic Value:* May contain proprietary metadata from cameras, editing software, or steganography tools.

fields.name: APP_Payload
fields.description:
**Application Data**

Application-specific payload. Displayed as ASCII text; non-printable characters indicate binary data.

*Forensic Value:* May contain hidden data, proprietary metadata, or software identifiers.

fields.name: UnknownSegment_Data
fields.condition: not ($SegmentMarker == 65504 or $SegmentMarker == 65505 or $SegmentMarker == 65506 or $SegmentMarker == 65516 or $SegmentMarker == 65517 or $SegmentMarker == 65518 or $SegmentMarker == 65534 or $SegmentMarker == 65499 or $SegmentMarker == 65472 or $SegmentMarker == 65473 or $SegmentMarker == 65474 or $SegmentMarker == 65475 or $SegmentMarker == 65476 or $SegmentMarker == 65501 or $SegmentMarker == 65498 or (65507 <= $SegmentMarker <= 65515) or $SegmentMarker == 65519)
fields.description:
**Unknown / Unhandled Segment**

A JPEG marker segment not specifically parsed by this configuration.

fields.name: UnknownPayload
fields.description:
**Segment Payload**

Raw data of this segment.

fields.name: CompressedImageData
fields.description:
**Compressed Image Data & EOI**

The entropy-coded (Huffman or arithmetic) compressed image data, followed by the End of Image marker (`FF D9`).

This data contains the actual visual content of the JPEG. It cannot be meaningfully parsed without decompression.

*Forensic Value:* Presence and integrity of the EOI marker at the end indicates the image data is complete. Missing EOI suggests truncation or corruption. Hidden data may be appended after the EOI marker (steganography, appended ZIP files, etc.).
